summary:
Picked up from the 15 Nov builder, which hit the usage limit right after its last change (shard belt widening 0.15). I made no code change on 16 Nov. I re-ran the whole check set on that final build and looked at the results myself, frame by frame, next to the reference.

IDLE (inner rings C and D). Cause: the old motion capture only sees the ring outline, and a symmetric ring looks the same whether it turns on through edge-on or turns back. So the fit folded the spins. The plot eyes/cd_angle_plot.png shows it: the old C turns back at t 2.7-3.4 s (-173..+240 deg/s, 4 reversals per 8 s), and the old D rocks with a net turn of 0 (-89..+91 deg/s, 16 reversals). That is the back-and-forth the user saw. Fix: C and D are now constant-rate flips about the rest camera's horizontal axis, measured from all 121 frames of Default Loop.mp4. C turns at -90 deg/s (a full turn per 4 s loop), D at +45 deg/s (half a turn). Each ring's starting tilt at tau 0 comes from fitting the ring edges in every loop frame, and the direction from which half darkens the orb as it passes in front. The motion is exactly periodic with no loop seam, and tau 0 still sits on F000. In eyes/idle_inner_pairs.jpg (engine next to reference every 0.2 s over the whole loop) every pair shows the same arrangement. Rings A and B were already constant-rate motions with no fold and are unchanged. `?idle=r10` restores the old motion capture.

HOLD. All rings run on one clock slowed to 0.2, the slow-motion share measured in the reference (A 0.19, B 0.19). The slow-down starts with the camera's lunge (F356-F372). C and D slow down in their new direction: -18 and +9 deg/s. The reference's C and D actually flip faster in the hold (about 135 deg/s), which the user already rejected as a "repeat" motion. So the video has no slow-motion factor for them, and they take the sculpture's measured 0.2, a uniform time remap.

A's quarters and B's halves keep exactly their ring's rotation. They only move apart radially in the ring's plane: A 0.6 m, B 0.1 m. There is no flex, tilt or per-piece spin. When the opened ring would leave the frame, the whole ring opens less by one shared amount. Ring A's opening therefore shrinks to about a third when A turns face-on at full zoom, and grows back smoothly (open issue 1).

SHARDS. They slow to 0.5 of idle speed, the reference's measured share, eased with the ring clock. Their belt no longer contracts during the zoom; it widens by 15% so no crystal passes through an opened piece.

VERIFIED on the final build. 60 Hz logs:
- Every ring's speed stays between 0.200 and 1.000 of its idle speed and never reverses. C -90 -> -18 and D +45 -> +9 deg/s, sign constant.
- Largest change in angular velocity between 60 Hz frames: A 8.4, B 6.2, C 3.05, D 1.53 deg/s.
- Pieces stay aligned with their ring: 2.4e-6 deg, 4.3e-5 m out of plane (float rounding).
- Shards 1 -> 0.5 -> 1 of idle speed with no jump; no crystal inside an opened piece (minimum clearance 0.10 m).
- Ring outlines stay inside the frame at every screen size tested; clicks still do nothing; typecheck passes.

Switches restore their builds bit-identically, except one live shot in mid-zoom (F358). That shot also differs when the main build is compared with itself, with the same 2e-4 camera offset and bit-equal ring rotations. Cause: the test harness reads pointer speed from the wall clock. So it is test noise, not a switch difference.
switches: ?idle=r10 : rings C / D get back their old motion-capture idle (with its loop tips). Also implied by ?hold=r10, ?hold=r11a, ?spin=s3, ?spin=f2

?spin=f2 : the integrated round-11 rotating hold exactly (flexA 1, per-piece frame guard, flipCD, clock 0.25, shards at ~94% with the belt contracting); with the implied ?idle=r10, ?spin=f2 alone equals the :5173 build
unchanged and re-verified on the final build: ?hold=r10, ?hold=r11a, ?spin=s3, ?aphase=r10 (with &spin=f2), and all-r10 ?env=projected&hold=r10&aphase=r10&ice=r10(&idle=r10) vs :5179
runtime knobs: __hero.debug.holdSpin.{slow 0.2, slow0 0.85, slow1 1.4, guardRing 1, shardSlow 0.5, shardContract 0, shardOut 0.15}

gates.gate: Idle C / D turn continuously, never rock
gates.numbers: C -90.000 and D +45.000 deg/s about their flip axis in every 60 Hz frame of 2 loops (no reversal, no change between frames). Old motion capture: C -173..+240 deg/s with 4 reversals per 8 s, D -89..+91 deg/s with 16 reversals and net 0 deg. Model matches the engine to 0.000 deg. Edge-fit score new vs old: C 0.1441 vs 0.1434, D 0.1493 vs 0.1481. Pairs every 0.2 s next to the reference match by eye.

gates.gate: Hold and release: every ring's motion continuous, never reversed (1/3/5/10/20 s holds, presses at tau 0/1.3/2.0/2.6, re-press 0.35/0.10 s, clicks)
gates.numbers: Speed as a share of each ring's idle speed: A 0.1999..1.0003, B 0.1999..1.0004, C/D 0.200..1.000; residual <= 0.0151. Largest change in angular velocity between 60 Hz frames: A 8.40, B 6.23, C 3.05, D 1.53 deg/s. Largest change in the speed share per frame: 0.0339.

gates.gate: Split pieces stay one ring (rotation equals the ring's, centroid in the ring plane)
gates.numbers: Every frame of every run: <= 2.4e-6 deg and <= 4.3e-5 m (float32). The integrated build had up to 0.499 m out of plane.

gates.gate: Inner rings slow down in the hold
gates.numbers: C -90 -> -18 deg/s, D +45 -> +9 deg/s (0.2, the measured A/B share). The reference's C/D flip at ~135 deg/s in the hold, 1.5x / 3x their idle speed, so the video gives no slower factor for them.

gates.gate: Shards slow down like the reference, no fly-through
gates.numbers: Engine 1 -> 0.50 -> 1 of idle speed, largest step 0.0212 per frame. Reference: 0.024-0.037 vs 0.050-0.064 rad/frame, about 0.5. Same tracker on the engine's frames: 0.87 vs the reference's 0.84. Fly-through test, 7359 frames: 0 hits, min clearance +0.100 m (integrated build: 48% of frames hit, -0.112 m).

gates.gate: H-G2 ring outlines inside the frame

gates.numbers: Click drivers 0, never holding. Ring step per 60 Hz frame for hold / release / re-press / release 2: 3.74 / 1.21 / 2.81 / 3.45 deg. No errors.

idle=r10 13/13; spin=f2 25/26 (17/17 with shards visible); hold=r10 24/26; hold=r11a 16/17; spin=s3 16/17; aphase=r10 24/26; all-r10 vs :5179 26/26. The only differing shots are live F358 mid-zoom, and the same build compared with itself gives the same difference (camera off 2e-4, ring rotations bit-equal).

16 Nov set ran beside other lanes' GPU jobs; each build swung 14-35 fps between runs. Median fps lane / main: rest 20.6/20.6, hold 17.9/20.4 (per-pair 1.00), collapse 20.2/29.6 (per-pair 0.75, range 0.53-1.25). Worst frame max 116.7/83.4 ms. Quiet 15 Nov set: rest 30.9/27.1, hold 23.6/23.1, collapse 31.9/28.8. CPU cost per update: rest 0.005/0.006 ms, hold 0.011/0.013, release 0.010/0.008.
tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.hero.json and -p .: exit 0, no output.

open_issues: Ring A's opening breathes with the tumble. Because the whole ring opens less as one unit when it would leave the frame, A's opening drops to about a third (0.6 -> 0.2 m) when it turns face-on and tall at full zoom, then grows back over about 2 s. The drift is smooth (~0.6 px per 60 Hz frame). The reference's arcs touch the frame edge at that moment, which H-G2 does not allow. The alternatives were one piece sliding in alone, or a camera that backs off.

The rotating hold follows the user's rule (lead decision 09:07), not A2's choreographed arrangement. The reference's pop / slab / lens poses are not reproduced; A2 only guides the opened shape and the camera.

C and D in the hold use the sculpture's measured 0.2 slow-motion factor. The video's own C/D motion in the hold is a fast face-on <-> flat flip (~135 deg/s) that the user rejected, so no per-ring slow factor for C/D exists in the reference.

Perf: the 16 Nov perf_probe set ran beside other lanes' GPU jobs and cannot resolve a few % (collapse per-pair median 0.75, range 0.53-1.25). The lane's per-frame CPU work measures the same as main, and the quiet 15 Nov set had the lane >= main in every phase. A quiet-machine A/B should be repeated at merge.

The test harness is not deterministic at the live mid-zoom shot (pointer speed taken from the wall clock), so F358 bit-identity can flicker between any two page sessions. Use tools/jcmp3.mjs (camera and ring-rotation differences) before calling a switch inexact.
B's halves part only 0.1 m (fix round 2's value). The engine's idle shards move ~0.67x the reference's on-screen speed (an older difference, not touched); the hold / idle ratio matches.
The water and foreground-floe items of the user's QC belong to the WATER lane. Nothing committed, deployed or uploaded; no .blend touched; lab :5174 stopped.
